question:
By interchanging the given two numbers (not digits) which of the following equation will be correct?

6 and 9

I. 7 x 9 + 6 - 5 ÷ 1 = 46

II. 3 x 9 + 6 - 8 ÷ 2 = 23
solution:
BODMAS Table:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db3d230a09fbbbf385a713651106df620079a920ae716ae92e9d71f7a5c0a9d1.png] 

Given equation: 

I. 7 x 9 + 6 - 5 ÷ 1 = 46

After interchanging the numbers 6 and 9 we get;

⇒ 7 × 6 + 9 − __**5 ÷ 1**__ = 46

⇒ **7 × 6** + 9 − 5 = 46

⇒ __**42**____** + 9**__ − 5 = 46

⇒ __**51 **____**− 5**__ = 46

⇒ 46 = 46

⇒ LHS = RHS

II. 3 x 9 + 6 - 8 ÷ 2 = 23

After interchanging the numbers 6 and 9 we get;

⇒ 3 × 6 + 9 − __**8 ÷ 2**__ = 23

⇒ __**3 × 6**__ + 9 − 4 = 23

⇒ __**18**____** + 9**__ − 4 = 23

⇒ **27**** − 4** = 23

⇒ 23 = 23

⇒ LHS = RHS

So, by interchanging the given two numbers, both I and II equation will be correct.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 3**".
